hero.title: How does your practice run participatory design?
hero.subtitle: Six questions for the NGOs, studios, consultancies and collectives doing this work. It takes about four minutes, and we share the benchmark findings back with you.

steps.section1Description: A little about your practice, so we can group answers by organization type and scale.
steps.section2Title: Section 2: Current tooling and pain points
steps.section2Description: Where your participatory process slows down today, and what you reach for when it does.
steps.section3Description: We are building a dedicated digital platform to streamline participatory design. These two answers tell us what to build first.
steps.emailDescription: That is everything we wanted to ask. If you would like a hand in what comes next, tell us where to reach you — that part is optional.

section1.label: What best describes your organization's primary role?

options.label: NGO / Non-Profit
Design Studio / Architecture Firm
Urban Consultancy / Strategic Agency
Hybrid / Citizen Collective

section1.label: What primary scale do your placemaking/participatory projects operate at?

options.label: Hyper-local (parks, pop-up interventions, single streets)
Neighborhood / Ward scale
City-wide / Strategic framework scale
Multi-city / International programs

section2.label: What is the single biggest bottleneck in your current participatory process?

options.label: Bridging digital & physical: Reaching diverse demographics (e.g., elderly vs. youth) across both on-site and online channels.
Data conversion: Turning qualitative community stories and sticky notes into GIS-ready spatial data or technical design specs.
Sustaining engagement: Keeping citizens updated and active during long municipal approval cycles.
Reporting & buy-in: Synthesizing complex inputs into compelling, data-driven reports that convince local government decision-makers.
Resource constraints: Lacking the budget or time to build custom digital tools for every new project.

section2.label: Which digital tools do you currently rely on most for community engagement?

options.label: Digital mapping/GIS tools (e.g., Maptionnaire, Felt, ArcGIS)
Online collaboration boards (e.g., Miro, Mural, Figma)
General survey tools (e.g., Typeform, Google Forms)
Social media & community messaging (e.g., WhatsApp groups, Instagram)
Proprietary / custom-built platforms

section3.label: Which feature would add the most immediate value to your practice?

options.label: AI-powered analysis: Automatic clustering of community feedback into spatial themes and actionable design requirements.
Hybrid sync: A mobile-friendly interface for field facilitators that instantly digitizes paper surveys and workshop maps.
Interactive spatial feedback: Intuitive, map-based engagement tools built specifically for non-technical residents.
Municipal reporting suite: One-click generation of policy-ready and technical design briefs for city officials.
Transparent project tracker: A public-facing dashboard showing citizens how their input directly shaped final designs.

section3.label: What is your organization's typical software/tool budget per project?

options.label: $0 (We strictly use free/open-source tools)
Under $500 per project
$500 – $2,000 per project
We subscribe to annual agency software licenses ($2,000+)

question.label: Would you be interested in shaping or testing this tool before launch?

options.label: Yes! I'd like early beta access and the opportunity to give feedback.
Yes, keep me updated on the launch and share the benchmark findings from this survey.
No, thanks.
